findings.evidence: GL level carries the full characterization — `isSemisimple_isUnipotent_unique` (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:169), `jordanDecomposition_spec` (:196), `eq_jordanDecomposition_iff` (:205), `semisimplePart_eq_self` (:319), `unipotentPart_eq_one_of_isSemisimple` (:328) — and `Functoriality.lean:111` shows `eq_jordanDecomposition_iff` is the load-bearing tool. The new file has no counterpart to any of them.
findings.fix: Add the point-level analogue of `TauCeti.GeneralLinearGroup.isSemisimple_isUnipotent_unique`: given `Commute s u`, `s * u = g`, and per-`M` `IsSemisimple (ofLinearEquiv (pointsAction M s))` / `IsUnipotent (ofLinearEquiv (pointsAction M u))`, conclude `s = semisimplePart k H K g ∧ u = unipotentPart k H K g`; then derive `semisimplePart_one`, `unipotentPart_one` and the self/one specializations. All ingredients are public: `Comodule.pointsAction` is a `MonoidHom` (PointsAction.lean:44) so `map_mul` transports the factorization and commutation componentwise, and `Tannaka.scalarExtensionComponent_ext` (Tannaka/Monoidal.lean:101) with `Tannaka.scalarExtensionComponent_fgPointTensorIso` and `fgPointTensorIsoEquiv.injective` turns componentwise equality back into equality of points.
findings.issue: `semisimplePart`/`unipotentPart` have no elimination principle: nothing states that a commuting factorization `g = s * u` acting semisimply/unipotently in every finite-dimensional comodule *is* this decomposition. Consequently `semisimplePart k H K 1 = 1`, `unipotentPart` of a point that is already semisimple, and the next roadmap step (functoriality under morphisms of affine groups) are unprovable from this interface; a consumer must re-enter `fgPointTensorIsoEquiv` and the tensor-iso layer.

Unlike the GL-level pair (which is primitive via `Classical.choose` and carries `jordanDecomposition_spec`/`eq_jordanDecomposition_iff`), this one asserts nothing — not even that its components commute or multiply to `g`.

findings.evidence: `Comodule.pointsAction_toLinearMap` is `@[simp]` (PointsAction.lean:50); `IsSemisimple` is stated on `GeneralLinearGroup K V` (Multiplicative.lean:60), and lines 163/172 of the new file rewrite with these two lemmas by hand.

No loop: LHS `ofLinearEquiv (pointsAction M (semisimplePart k H K g))` reduces to `GeneralLinearGroup.semisimplePart (ofLinearEquiv (pointsAction M g))`, the same normal form the `endOfPoint_*` simp lemmas reach through the `@[simp]` `Comodule.pointsAction_toLinearMap`.
findings.issue: `ofLinearEquiv_pointsAction_semisimplePart` and `ofLinearEquiv_pointsAction_unipotentPart` (line 147) are the characteristic identifications in the `GeneralLinearGroup` unit form — the form in which `GeneralLinearGroup.IsSemisimple`/`IsUnipotent` are stated and in which the file itself uses them — but are not `@[simp]`, while the coerced linear-map versions `endOfPoint_semisimplePart`/`endOfPoint_unipotentPart` are.

summary: The reconstructed points come with representation-wise identifications but no uniqueness/characterization lemma, so nothing about a concrete point's parts can be proved without reopening the Tannakian construction; `jordanDecomposition` is an inert pair with only two `rfl` projections.
